newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy bought marks and dollars -- Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy bought marks and dollars -- Fazio.

text.p: The Bank of Italy has bought dollars and German marks to repay some $12-13 billion worth of debt accumulated when the lira crashed out of the European exchange rate mechanism in 1992, bank governor Antonio Fazio said.
"I cannot deny that we have been buying reserves, supporting the mark and dollar exchange rate," Fazio told a parliamentary budget commission on Thursday.
"When you see data published at the end of the year, you will see that $12-13 billion of debts that we picked up in 1992 have disappeared," he said.
"It is true that this buying has prevented the exchange rate from (rising). If we hadn't bought, the exchange rate against the mark would be different."
The lira has risen steadily against the mark in the past weeks, but recently stalled between the 990-1,000 level per mark.
Fazio did not indicate when the Bank of Italy had been in the market. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
